findings.rationale: WA is the only client whose update statistics stand clearly apart. Its update norm is about 2-2.8x the median in rounds 1-9 and its direction matches the consensus almost exactly in rounds 1-2 (cos = 1.0), which is consistent with a scaled (manipulated) upload from the start. The norm z-score is +4.6 across the full run, and WA is a large client (n_train 11181), so this deviation is not sampling noise. The norm ratio later falls toward ~1.25 and the cosine decays, so the pattern is not a clean constant scaling; the confidence is moderate. Other screens (performance, drift, feature tails, subgroup O/E) showed no consistent WA anomaly; its one large subgroup O/E outlier did not reproduce on re-query.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then re-queried suspects. Only WA shows a consistent, large-client anomaly: update norms about 2-2.8x the median in early rounds with cos near 1, flagged at z=+4.6. I report it as poisoning (scaled update) from round 1 with moderate confidence. WI (norm z=+3.3, cosine decaying to negative late in training) is a weaker lead that I did not report, since it is not confirmed by a second independent statistic. Other single outliers did not reproduce on re-query (e.g. WA and NY income-subgroup O/E ratios, AL citl drift, WV/GU/DC/VI feature tails, which are consistent with noise on small clients). Budget was fully spent (20.0 epsilon).
